items.title: Norfolk and Suffolk ICB sizes its CVD prevention and optimisation service at £12.4m
items.summary: NHS Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board has published a second market engagement notice for a single, digitally enabled cardiovascular disease prevention and optimisation pathway, starting with hypertension and lipid management, at an estimated £12.4m.

items.title: STRIDE-RCT: cancer-detecting blood tests to be offered to 20,000 NHS patients via 200 GP practices
items.summary: The STRIDE-RCT trial will offer blood tests for early cancer signals to over 20,000 patients aged 45+ with abdominal symptoms at 200 GP surgeries. First tests: Proteotype (Enlighten), Pinpoint AI (PinPoint) and Mercy Bioanalytics (Halo); more may be added. Source: Evening Standard.

items.title: NMC confirms nursing students must complete one community placement
items.summary: Plans to ensure nursing students undertake at least one practice learning placement in the community have been approved by the Nursing and Midwifery Council’s (NMC) governing body.

items.title: Second phase of chickenpox vaccination programme underway
items.summary: The second phase of the chickenpox vaccination schedule began this month, marking the start of the catch-up programme. From January this year, GP practices started to offer a combined MMRV vaccine at 12 months and 18 months of age to add chickenpox (varicella) to the protections against measles, mumps and rubella.

items.title: Decline in women using hormonal contraception, national survey shows
items.summary: Fewer young women are using hormonal contraception than a decade ago, a large British survey has found. Half of women aged 16-24 use hormonal contraception compared with 65% 10 years ago, the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4) found.

items.title: Nurses need ‘supported route’ into general practice, urges report
items.summary: The government must ensure nurses have a ‘supported route’ into general practice nursing, with proper induction, supervision and training opportunities to help strengthen the workforce, a report has urged.

items.title: GPs have almost 120 more patients each than in 2015, finds Pulse analysis
items.summary: There are almost 120 more patients for each fully-qualified permanent GP in England than in 2015, despite Government efforts to increase the workforce, a Pulse analysis has found.

items.title: Health secretary issues NHS warning following 5k heat-related deaths this summer
items.summary: Health secretary Yvette Cooper has called on the NHS to strengthen planning for summer after figures showed more than 5,000 deaths were linked to a series of heatwaves this year.

items.title: Next week: Don’t miss our final Nursing in Practice Virtual event of 2026
items.summary: With winter pressures building and patient demand increasing, now is the time to refresh your clinical knowledge ahead of the busy months to come.

items.title: Antidepressant batch recalled over incorrect strength labelling
items.summary: Quadrant Pharmaceuticals is recalling a batch of the antidepressant Brintellix (vortioxetine) after 5mg tablets were supplied in sealed cartons labelled as containing 10mg tablets. The labelling error, which affects an unknown number of packs, is limited to parallel imported products.

items.title: How to manage hydration and frailty in a warming climate
items.summary: As heatwaves become more frequent and intense, protecting older adults from dehydration must become a priority for frailty management, medicines safety and care home practice.

items.title: Ebola Bundibugyo: what nurses need to know
items.summary: Given the unprecedented nature of the ongoing Ebola outbreak in parts of Africa, the virus has been in the news regularly over the past few months. More than 11,000 people have been infected so far and thousands have died, with the outbreak on track to become the largest of its kind on record. The epidemic...

items.title: Incentivise GPs to provide annual health check to every patient, says DAUK
items.summary: Doctors’ Association UK (DAUK) has proposed that every patient should be offered an annual health check with their GP in their birthday month. Although it would cost the Government an estimated £3.2bn, the DAUK said annual reviews ‘could save the NHS as a whole ‘billions of pounds’.

items.title: New GP event to focus on tackling CVD inequalities in deprived communities
items.summary: A new event exploring how GPs and their teams can tackle cardiovascular disease (CVD) inequalities and improve outcomes for patients in deprived communities will launch in March next year.

items.title: GPs refuse to endorse local ADHD service offer over shared care concerns
items.summary: A group of LMCs has refused to endorse an ICB’s adult ADHD local enhanced service (LES), citing concerns about work being ‘transferred’ to general practice, and insufficient payments for GPs.

items.title: GPs must challenge NHSE’s redefinition of QOF
items.summary: Pulse editor Sofia Lind warns against letting NHS England get away with redefining the purpose of the Quality and Outcomes Framework Our major investigation into how local enhanced services for prescribing and managing tirzepatide for obesity have disappeared just one year on made the headlines this week.

items.title: Nursing in Practice Podcast: Navigating the chickenpox vaccination programme
items.summary: The latest episode of the Nursing in Practice Podcast welcomes a senior lecturer in nursing from City St George’s University to talk about the newly introduced varicella vaccination, also known as chickenpox.

items.title: Exclusive: New nursing advisory councils to give practice nurses ‘a voice’
items.summary: Local nursing advisory councils are being developed to help give general practice nurses (GPNs) a voice in sharing concerns and shaping policy at a regional and national level, Nursing in Practice can reveal.

items.title: Learning disability nursing course suspended amid recruitment challenges
items.summary: The University of West of England (UWE) Bristol has suspended its undergraduate learning disability nursing programme amid difficulties recruiting students onto the course.

items.title: ICBs fail to commission services for GPs to offer Wegovy for cardiovascular risk
items.summary: Exclusive Not a single ICB in England has confirmed they currently meet a statutory responsibility to commission services for GPs to prescribe and monitor Wegovy (semaglutide) for cardiovascular risk, six months after NICE recommended its rollout, Pulse has learnt.

items.title: Government appoints chair for social care pay talks
items.summary: The government has appointed House of Lords member and former Unison general secretary Baroness Christina McAnea to chair negotiations on pay and conditions for care workers in England.

items.title: ‘Dementia care should start at diagnosis, long before a crisis’
items.summary: People living with dementia and their families are too often left without support until they reach crisis point. Dementia UK’s Charlotte Lillford-Wildman calls for a national standard of care that starts at diagnosis and continues as needs change.

items.title: PCRS webinar: health inequalities in asthma care for children, 30 November
items.summary: Primary Care Respiratory Society webinar for UK healthcare professionals on 30 November, 19:00 to 20:00, on asthma care inequalities, diagnosis and urgent to primary care working.

items.title: PCRS webinar: SNOMED coding in primary care respiratory conditions, 10 December
items.summary: Primary Care Respiratory Society webinar on 10 December at 18:00 on why accurate SNOMED coding matters for respiratory conditions in primary care.

items.title: Nurses in Northern Ireland to take industrial action over pay
items.summary: Nurses working across Northern Ireland’s Health and Social Care (HSC) have voted ‘overwhelmingly’ in favour of taking industrial action amid ongoing concerns over pay. The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has announced that some 93% of voting members have backed both strike action and action short of strike.

items.title: People applying for PIP ‘should not pay GPs to provide additional evidence’, review says
items.summary: A major Government review has called for changes to the way GPs provide evidence for disability benefit claims.

items.title: NHS Pension Scheme: what could proposed changes mean for nurses?
items.summary: With the government having launched a consultation on proposed changes to the NHS Pension Scheme, Nursing in Practice explores what the proposals mean for nurses and their families, what we know about workplace pensions among general practice nurses (GPNs) and how the profession can have its say.

items.title: GPs could see mandatory training burden reduced under NHS England plans
items.summary: GPs could see a reduction in mandatory training requirements under NHS England plans to reform statutory and mandatory training across the health service.

items.title: Nursing organisations oppose closure of NMC oversight group
items.summary: Nursing and midwifery organisations have called on the Professional Standards Authority (PSA) to reconsider its decision to close the Independent Oversight Group (IOG) for the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC).

items.title: Why GPs can’t prescribe Mounjaro; and new suicide warnings for starting SSRIs
items.summary: The new episode of Pulse in Focus: The Podcast for GPs is now live and available on all podcast platforms. Senior journalist Maya Dhillon talks to Pulse deputy news editor Anna Colivicchi about her new investigation into funding cuts for tirzepatide provision in general practice.

items.title: ARRS roles expanded primary care capacity without reducing GP workload, finds study
items.summary: The additional roles reimbursement scheme (ARRS) has expanded primary care capacity but there is little evidence that it has directly reduced GPs’ workload, a study has suggested.

items.title: NHS rolls out training to tackle unauthorised access to patient records
items.summary: GP practice staff are among those who can access updated NHS training being rolled out this week as part of a crackdown on unauthorised access to patient records.

items.title: ‘Qualifying as a GP should be the beginning of opportunity, not uncertainty’
items.summary: Outgoing RCGP First5 chair Dr Toyosi Adeniji reflects on three years of supporting newly-qualified GPs, and how the landscape of general practice has shifted in that time When I became national First5 chair back in 2023, one of my priorities was to help colleagues navigate one of the most significant transitions in…

items.title: Daily Viagra-like pill shows promise in early Alzheimer’s disease
items.summary: A Viagra-like daily pill that increases blood flow to the brain has shown promising results in slowing the progression of Alzheimer’s disease in phase 3 trials.

items.title: ‘Significant concerns’ remain over NMC performance as oversight group closes
items.summary: The Professional Standards Authority (PSA) has said it continues to have ‘significant concerns’ about the performance of the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC), following the final meeting of the group overseeing the regulator’s response to serious issues raised regarding its culture and governance.

items.title: UK GPs experience highest workload stress, international survey finds
items.summary: Nearly seven in 10 GPs report suffering from work-related stress, the highest rate among comparable countries, a think-tank has found.

items.title: MPs urge government to reimburse GPs for hosting district nurses
items.summary: MPs have urged the government to consider changing rules which penalise GPs for hosting district nurses and other community services in their surgeries.

items.title: ICBs should be required to consult LMCs on primary care commissioning, say GPs
items.summary: ICBs should be required to consult LMCs on any further changes to primary care commissioning, GP leaders have said. GP representatives overwhelmingly carried a motion at the BMA’s England LMC conference calling for ICBs to consult LMCs on this issue.

items.title: Dedicated staffing budget needed to make general practice pay rises ‘more affordable’
items.summary: The government has been urged to introduce a ringfenced staffing budget to help make pay rises ‘more affordable’ within general practice. A new report published by our sister title Management in Practice highlights the constraints faced by GP practices when it comes to annual pay rises, including for practice nurses.

items.title: Investigation: How withdrawing local GP funding for Mounjaro is jeopardising access
items.summary: As part of our new investigation The Weight of GLP-1 Cuts, Anna Colivicchi looks at what the withdrawal of local services for GPs to provide and monitor Mounjaro means for practices and patients ‘People who meet the national NHS criteria will be able to access Mounjaro through their usual GP practice,’ says a message…

items.title: ‘Nurses must find a way to counter narratives being framed around advanced practice’
items.summary: Amid growing scrutiny of advanced practice and concerns about patient safety, nurse academic and advanced nurse practitioner Dr Helen Anderson explores the tensions behind the debate, how professional boundaries and professional identities have shaped the development of advanced practice, and why nursing leaders must…

items.title: District nurse support helps Wolverhampton care home avoid unnecessary referrals
items.summary: An ‘outstanding’ care home in Wolverhampton has seen district nurses offer training to its nursing team in a move that hopes to help avoid unnecessary referrals and support faster treatment.

items.title: AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial hopes to ‘free up staff time’
items.summary: Thousands of women are set to take part in the world’s largest artificial intelligence (AI) assisted breast cancer screening trial, NHS England has confirmed.

items.title: NHS chief defends plans to exclude GPs as ICB decision makers
items.summary: NHS England has defended plans not to require integrated care boards (ICBs) to include GP representatives. GP representation in decision-making may lie outside the ‘construct’ of ICBs, the NHS England’s chief executive told MPs last week.

items.title: LMCs oppose mandatory A&G being used as barrier to referral
items.summary: GP leaders across England have opposed mandatory advice and guidance (A&G), single point of access or triage processes being used as barriers to clinically indicated referral.

items.title: Interview: Antimicrobial resistance ‘is here and already posing a threat’
items.summary: It’s World Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Awareness Week (18 to 24 November), and we spoke with Professor Diane Ashiru-Oredope, lead pharmacist for healthcare-associated infections and AMR at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

items.title: Nursing Support Workers’ Day: ‘We protect dignity and make a difference every day’
items.summary: Care home assistant practitioner Sarah Omode highlights the value, recognition and development of nursing support workers to mark an annual day of recognition – Nursing Support Workers’ Day – on Monday 23 November.

items.title: Exclusive: Most ICBs withdraw services for GPs to prescribe and monitor Mounjaro
items.summary: Exclusive Most ICBs across England have withdrawn locally commissioned services for GPs to prescribe and monitor Mounjaro, a Pulse investigation has found.

items.title: Future GP contracts should incorporate LES funding, say LMCs
items.summary: Future national GP contracts should incorporate existing local enhanced services (LESs), with recurrent funding attached, GP leaders have said.

items.title: Dr Tom Black: ‘The Government hates GPs with a visceral passion’
items.summary: Pulse LIVE Belfast saw Pulse editor Sofia Lind sit down with former NI BMA chair Dr Tom Black to discuss the recently agreed GP contract, funding, collective action, and whether the profession is moving any closer towards a Plan B model of private and and public healthcare You have previously been involved with the…

items.title: How this nursing team is making childhood vaccinations more accessible
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Low flu vaccine uptake among toddlers as GP visits for flu-like illness rise
items.summary: Only around a third (37%) of two- and three-years-olds have been vaccinated against the flu, leaving thousands of young children at risk, the UK Health and Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned.

items.title: GPC instructed to negotiate uplift to core funding to offset list cleansing
items.summary: GP leaders have demanded that the BMA negotiates an equivalent uplift to core GP funding to compensate practices for the loss of income caused by NHS England’s ongoing list-cleansing drive.

items.title: NMC warns AI-generated referrals are complicating fitness to practise assessments
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in fitness to practise (FtP) referrals and is, in some cases, making it difficult for the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) to assess whether regulatory action is needed.

items.title: GPs should be reimbursed for hosting district nurses, MPs urge
items.summary: The government must ensure GP practices are reimbursed for hosting other professions such as district nurses and community services if it wants its neighbourhood shift to succeed, an influential committee of MPs has urged.

items.title: NHS Property Services should face ‘independent review’, say MPs
items.summary: The Government has been urged to commission a review into NHS Property Services (NHSPS) due to ‘consistent concerns’ about its ownership of GP practice premises.

items.title: Government urged to create loan scheme for GPs to invest in premises upgrades
items.summary: The Government has been urged to give GPs access to Government-backed borrowing to help GPs invest in premises upgrades, as part of a ‘GP capital and revenue investment strategy’.

items.title: NMC drops plans to reduce nursing programme hours
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has dropped plans to change student nursing programme hours after a consultation revealed a lack of support.

items.title: Managing hyperkalaemia – five top tips for GPs
items.summary: As part of our series showcasing Pulse LIVE and Virtual sessions highlights, GP diabetes and kidney specialist Dr Kevin Fernando provides five practical pointers on how to manage a case of hyperkalaemia Note the case discussed in this article is fictional and created for educational purposes Hyperkalaemia is commonly…

items.title: Sleep disorders: Top ten advice and guidance requests
items.summary: Consultant neurologist Dr Kirstie Anderson, consultant in sleep and respiratory medicine Dr Alanna Hare and GP Dr Elspeth Wise discuss ten typical requests to advice and guidance for sleep disorders and how they should be managed Note all 10 requests are fictional and developed for educational purposes 1.

items.title: First cross-party parliamentary group dedicated to nursing launched
items.summary: A cross-party parliamentary group dedicated to the nursing profession has been launched for the first time. The All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) for Nursing has been established in Westminster, with MPs and nurses coming together for an inaugural meeting this week to discuss priorities and issues raised by nurses.

items.title: Government seeks nurse views on proposed NHS Pension Scheme changes
items.summary: Nurses and other healthcare staff are being asked to have their say on proposed changes to the NHS Pension Scheme. The government has today launched a public consultation focusing on changes to the scheme which are set to come into force from April 2027.

items.title: Government launches consultation on changes to the NHS Pension Scheme
items.summary: The Government has launched a public consultation seeking views on proposed changes to the NHS Pension Scheme, which are set to come into force from April next year.

items.title: Neighbourhood support teams must be ‘built around nurses’
items.summary: Nursing organisations have stressed that new neighbourhood support teams need to be ‘built around’ district and community nurses who are ‘already doing the work’.

items.title: Call for evidence to determine future of the NHS constitution
items.summary: The Government has launched a public call for evidence to help ‘understand the impact’ of the NHS Constitution for England. This includes asking the public if they support having an NHS constitution at all.

items.title: List-cleansing to have ‘significant’ implications for ARRS budgets, GP leaders warn
items.summary: NHS England’s GP list-cleansing drive will have ‘significant’ implications for additional roles reimbursement scheme (ARRS) budgets, GP leaders and experts have warned.

items.title: ADHD and autism to feature at free Pulse virtual event
items.summary: GPs are invited to a free virtual event next month focussed on ADHD, autism and mental health in primary care.

items.title: NICE approves capsule sponge test for oesophageal cancer in primary care
items.summary: NICE has approved the use of a capsule sponge test to detect oesophageal cancer and Barrett’s oesophagus in primary care and community settings. Two tests – Cytosponge and EndoSign – have been recommended for use on the NHS under new draft guidance.

items.title: QICN award to recognise prescribing students in social care nursing
items.summary: The Queen’s Institute of Community Nursing (QICN) has launched a new academic prize recognising outstanding students undertaking the prescribing programme for adult social care nurses.

items.title: NHS e-learning updated to support people rough sleeping this winter
items.summary: NHS e-learning resources on homelessness have been updated to help GPs and other healthcare staff support people experiencing rough sleeping as part of the Prime Ministers ambition to get people off the streets this winter.

items.title: Resource GPs properly to tackle vaccination decline, House of Lords committee says
items.summary: The Government should review primary care funding for childhood vaccination to tackle declining uptake and address stark inequalities, a report from a House of Lords special inquiry has recommended.

items.title: New ‘neighbourhood support teams’ to keep almost two million out of hospital
items.summary: New neighbourhood support teams aim to keep 1.8 million people out of hospital through ‘dedicated and personalised’ care in the community, the health secretary has announced.

items.title: Patient death raises concerns about community nurses’ access to medical records
items.summary: A coroner has raised concerns about some community nurses’ lack of access to relevant medical records when undertaking invasive procedures following the death of a patient whose catheterisation resulted in haematuria.

items.title: How not to miss: Scabies
items.summary: In the first of a new series looking at conditions that can easily be overlooked or misattributed, GP Dr Keith Hopcroft describes how a case of scabies is initially treated as eczema – and explores some of the other pitfalls that can lead to a delayed diagnosis of this contagious infection Note cases in this series...

items.title: One in three internationally educated nurses ‘never been promoted’ in UK
items.summary: More than a third (34%) of internationally educated nurses and midwives have never been promoted, including one in five (21%) of those with at least 10 years’ experience in the UK, a survey has revealed.

items.title: Redefining obesity would be a weight off my mind
items.summary: Copperfield wonders whether, if changing BMI to waist circumference can make so many people healthier on paper, there are other areas of general practice where a simple change of metric could work wonders Some good news for once. That obesity timebomb they keep talking about may be just a damp squib.

items.title: Improve vaccine access for people with lung conditions, taskforce concludes
items.summary: Too many people with lung conditions are missing out on vital vaccines, according to a taskforce calling for better education and easier access. A survey of more than 2,200 adults with lung conditions commissioned by the Taskforce for Lung Health found many did not see themselves at risk.

items.title: ‘Neighbourhood support teams’ to work with GPs to keep patients out of hospital
items.summary: New ‘neighbourhood support teams’ will work with GPs and provide ‘dedicated and personalised’ care to vulnerable patients to help keep them out of hospital, the health secretary has announced today.

items.title: Practice nurse shortages undermining childhood vaccination efforts, Lords warn
items.summary: A shortage of nurses working in general practice means those among the workforce have less time to speak to parents about childhood vaccinations and is ultimately contributing to falling immunisation rates, a report has warned.

items.title: GMC ‘erroneously’ gave identifiable FtP data to national newspaper
items.summary: The GMC has ‘erroneously’ shared doctors’ personal identifiable data with a national newspaper, including their names and details of allegations against them, the BMA has said.

items.title: Government urged to introduce maximum waiting times for CAMHS by 2028
items.summary: The Government should introduce maximum waiting times from the point of referral for Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) by 2028, a Government review has recommended.

items.title: How this nurse leader is taking primary care beyond the surgery walls
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Two funded innovation programmes open to primary care and community nurses
items.summary: The Queen’s Institute of Community Nursing (QICN) has two funded innovation opportunities open to primary care and community nurses wanting to help improve the health and wellbeing of others.

items.title: GPs should not issue long-term fit notes from next year, recommends landmark review
items.summary: GPs should no longer have responsibility for issuing fit notes for long-term sickness absence, according to a major review of youth unemployment in the UK. Alan Milburn’s report, published today, said long-term fit note responsibility should be moved ‘out of general practice’ from 2027.

items.title: Renewed call for long Covid recognition as nurses suffer ‘debilitating effects’ six years on
items.summary: A nursing union has renewed calls for the government to formally recognise long Covid as nurses continue to suffer ‘debilitating effects’ six years after the pandemic began.

items.title: Coroner flags risk of deaths from nurse shortages
items.summary: An inquest into the death of an 83-year-old man whose hip operation was repeatedly cancelled has prompted a coroner to warn that nursing shortages in the NHS could cost more lives.

items.title: GP willingness to use A&G depends on it being ‘timely and clinically useful’
items.summary: The willingness of GPs to use advice and guidance (A&G) depends on whether they receive timely and clinically useful responses, researchers have found.

items.title: Letter calls for patient needs to be prioritised over cost in continence care
items.summary: Continence care must be driven by patient needs and outcomes instead of costs, an open letter signed by the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) and others has urged.

items.title: Up to £6m saved through GP list-cleansing to be returned to ‘most impacted’ practices
items.summary: Government officials have confirmed that up to £6m saved from GP list-cleansing will be returned to ‘practices most impacted’ by the process, the BMA has revealed.

items.title: ‘We can leave the surgery, but can we ever escape our patients?’
items.summary: Dr Burnt Out on the occupational hazard that is being recognised by your patients outside the GP surgery ‘Hello doctor.’ These are two words that you do not necessarily want to hear when you are out and about doing your daily business.

items.title: UK-wide framework to ‘strengthen and celebrate’ nurses’ contribution to public health
items.summary: A new UK-wide framework focused on the contribution of nurses in public health hopes to provide a ‘common language’ to describe, strengthen and celebrate the impact of the profession.

items.title: ‘Now is the time to build on nurses’ public health legacy and leadership’
items.summary: England’s deputy chief public health nurse Professor Jamie Waterall explores how nurses and midwives can build on their public health legacy, using a new UK-wide framework to strengthen leadership, tackle health inequalities and help more people live well for longer.

items.title: HRT prescribing rose 12% last year but inequalities persist
items.summary: Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) prescribing in England has risen by 12%, however the statistic comes amid warnings patients face an ‘unfair postcode lottery’ over access.

items.title: Over 300 reports of ‘unauthorised access’ to medical records made this year
items.summary: The Information Commission’s Office (ICO) is urging NHS England to tackle unauthorised access to patient records, after it revealed it received over 300 reports of ‘unauthorised access’ from health organisations so far this year.

items.title: BMA must support GP practices who want to leave GMS, says NI LMCs
items.summary: LMC representatives at the BMA’s annual NI LMCs conference voted through a motion calling on the BMA to support practices in leaving the GMS contract and ‘implement a plan B’.

items.title: More health and social care workers to be balloted on strike action in Northern Ireland
items.summary: Around 4,000 health and social care workers in Northern Ireland are to be balloted on industrial action amid an ongoing dispute over pay, the union Unite has announced. Unite will ballot its members across 10 employers in Northern Ireland from Monday 23 November until Monday 14 December.

items.title: Only a clear national scope of practice can set safe limits for physician associates, says BMA
items.summary: The BMA has published new ‘red lines’ for physician associates (PAs), which say only a ‘clear’ national scope of practice can set ‘safe limits’ for their work.

items.title: Oral thrush: what nurses need to know
items.summary: Oral thrush is often managed as a minor ailment, but recurrent episodes can signal underlying issues such as medicines-related harm, raised blood sugars or immunosuppression.

items.title: New life-extending anal cancer treatment available on NHS, NICE confirms
items.summary: A life-extending advanced anal cancer treatment has been approved by NICE and is available immediately on the NHS. It is estimated around 250 people in England are set to benefit from the new targeted treatment for anal cancer which has spread and cannot be removed through surgery.

items.title: Practice nurses urged to champion veteran health scheme
items.summary: In the lead up to Remembrance Day, practice nurses are being encouraged to champion a health scheme to provide the best possible care and treatment for Armed Forces veterans.
